classification.difficultyReason: Requires converting scaled axes, reading the line both ways, finding a rate of change in t/ha per 100 mm, a residual from the line, and extrapolating with that rate.

content.prompt: The scatterplot shows the annual rainfall and wheat yield of 10 farms in Western Australia. A line of best fit has been drawn for these points.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Use the line of best fit to estimate the yield of a farm that receives 450 mm of rainfall.

answer.worked: From 450 mm on the rainfall axis, read vertically to the line of best fit, then horizontally to the yield axis: approximately 2.1 t/ha.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Use the line of best fit to estimate the rainfall needed for a yield of 3 t/ha.

answer.worked: From 3 t/ha on the yield axis, read horizontally to the line of best fit, then vertically to the rainfall axis: approximately 570 mm.

children.label: c
children.prompt: By about how much does the estimated yield increase for each extra 100 mm of rainfall?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{At 400 mm the line gives }&1.75\text{ t/ha}\\\text{At 500 mm the line gives }&2.5\text{ t/ha}\\2.5-1.75&=0.75\text{ t/ha}\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: One farm received 600 mm of rainfall. How much lower was its yield than the yield estimated by the line?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Line at 600 mm}&=3.25\text{ t/ha}\\\text{Farm's yield}&=2.75\text{ t/ha}\\3.25-2.75&=0.5\text{ t/ha}\end{align*}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: Use your answer to part c to estimate the yield of a farm that receives 800 mm of rainfall.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Line at 700 mm}&=4\text{ t/ha}\\\text{Extra 100 mm}&:+0.75\text{ t/ha}\\4+0.75&=4.75\text{ t/ha}\end{align*}$$
